examples.ko: 책의 첫 장을 맛보기로 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I read the first chapter of the book as a taster.
The trial lesson of this course is free.

examples.ko: 시식 코너에서 맛보기용 작은 컵을 받았어요.
examples.en: At the sampling corner I got a small sample cup.
A trailer is only a taste of the movie.

examples.ko: 먼저 맛보기만 하고 마음에 들면 살게요.
examples.en: I'll just try a little first, and if I like it, I'll buy it.

examples.ko: 신제품 맛보기 행사에 사람들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up at the new product tasting event.

explain: 음식뿐 아니라 책, 영화, 수업처럼 전체를 사기 전에 조금만 미리 보여 주는 것에도 두루 써요. 음식을 먹어 보는 '시식'보다 쓰임이 넓고, '미리보기'와 가까운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I watched the preview video first and then decided.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전체를 보기 전에 일부만 먼저 보여 주는 영상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A video that shows only a part before you see the whole thing.

phrases.en: This is just a sample, so the amount is small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본 상품이 아니라 조금만 써 보라고 만든 것에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to something made as a small trial rather than the full product.

phrases.en: I'll try the sample class first and then sign up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본 수업을 시작하기 전에 조금만 미리 들어 보는 수업을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short trial class you take before enrolling in the full course.

explain_en: It covers not only food but anything that gives a small preview before you commit, such as a book, movie or class. It is broader than '시식', which is only about tasting food, and is close in feel to '미리보기'.

examples.en: The next step is signing the contract.

examples.ko: 협상이 깨지면 파업으로 가는 게 수순이에요.
examples.en: If the negotiation falls through, a strike is the expected next step.

examples.ko: 바둑에서는 수순에 따라 결과가 크게 달라져요.
examples.en: In baduk, the result changes a lot depending on the order of moves.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실적이면 승진은 당연한 수순이라고 생각해요.
examples.en: With results like this, I think a promotion is the natural next step.

examples.ko: 먼저 밟아야 할 수순을 정리해 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote out the steps we need to take first.

examples.ko: 문제가 생기면 보고부터 하는 수순으로 일해요.
examples.en: We work in an order where we report first when a problem comes up.

explain: 원래 바둑이나 장기에서 수를 두는 차례를 말하는데, 일상에서는 일이 예상대로 이어지는 순서를 가리켜요. '순서'보다 '이렇게 흘러가겠구나' 하는 느낌이 있어서 '당연한 수순', '다음 수순'처럼 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The company is going through the usual steps toward restructuring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 절차나 예상되는 흐름대로 일을 진행한다는 뜻이에요. 뉴스에서 자주 쓰고, 일이 자연스럽게 그쪽으로 간다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means proceeding along an expected or set course of steps. It is common in the news and suggests things are naturally heading that way.

explain_en: Formal — next step in a course of action (다음 수순) It originally refers to the order of moves in baduk or janggi, but in daily life it points to the order in which things proceed as expected. Compared with '순서', it carries a feeling of 'this is how it will naturally go', so '당연한 수순' and '다음 수순' are common.

dis.h: formal; steps in a procedure or process
gh: everyday word; order in a line or list

p.n: The everyday word is plainer and less technical.

t90.ax: The next step is signing the contract.

examples.en: The new product demonstration is held tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ko: 이번 시연회는 본 행사 전의 예행연습이라고 생각하세요.
examples.en: Please think of this demo as a rehearsal before the main event.
I was invited to a demo and saw a robot for the first time.
The team members prepared all night before the demonstration.
The screen suddenly went off during the demonstration.

examples.ko: 시연회에서 앱 사용법을 직접 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: At the demo, they showed us how to use the app in person.

explain: 제품이나 기술이 실제로 어떻게 작동하는지 직접 보여 주는 자리예요. 영화를 미리 보여 주는 행사는 '시사회'라고 해서 달라요. '시연회를 열다', '시연회에 참석하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The company held a demonstration event for the new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주최하는 쪽에서 시연회를 마련할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the organizer's side when setting up a demonstration event.

phrases.en: Reporters attended the demonstration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보러 가는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of those who go to see it.

phrases.en: I received an invitation to the demonstration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시연회에 오라고 보내는 초대 문서를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an invitation sent to invite people to a demonstration.

explain_en: An event held to show a new product or app (회사에서 새 앱의 시연회를 열어서 구경하러 갔어요.) This is an event that shows in person how a product or technology actually works. An event that previews a film is called '시사회', which is different. You say '시연회를 열다' or '시연회에 참석하다'.

t90.ax: The screen suddenly went off during the demonstration.

examples.ko: 학교 강당에서 영사기로 영화를 틀어 줬어요.
examples.en: They played a movie with a projector in the school hall.
The sound of an old projector running feels warm and nostalgic.

examples.ko: 영사기 불빛이 어두운 극장 벽에 번졌어요.
examples.en: The projector light spread across the wall of the dark theater.
I looked at an old projector at the museum.

examples.ko: 영사기는 필름을 한 장씩 빠르게 비춰요.
examples.en: A projector shines film frames one after another very quickly.

examples.ko: 영사기에 필름을 거는 일을 아저씨가 맡았어요.
examples.en: The man took charge of loading the film onto the projector.

explain: 극장이나 옛날 학교에서 필름 영화를 비추는 기계를 떠올리는 말이에요. 요즘 회의나 수업에서 화면을 비추는 기기는 보통 '프로젝터'나 '빔프로젝터'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 영사기를 켜고 영화를 보여 주셨어요.
phrases.en: The teacher turned on the projector and showed us a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영사기'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common verb pairing with '영사기'.

phrases.en: The sound of the projector echoed in the quiet room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 필름 영사기가 돌아가는 소리를 떠올리게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It brings to mind the sound of an old film projector running.

phrases.en: I showed the materials with a projector in the meeting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영사기'는 옛날 필름 기계 느낌이고, '프로젝터'는 요즘 회의나 수업에서 쓰는 기기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '영사기' feels like an old film machine, while '프로젝터' is the modern device for meetings and classes.

explain_en: Older device projecting film in cinemas. It brings to mind the machine that shows film movies in theaters or old schools. For the device used in meetings or classes today, people usually say '프로젝터' or '빔프로젝터'.

t90.ax: I looked at an old projector at the museum.

examples.en: The new president's inauguration is held tomorrow.
Many guests came to the inauguration.
I watched the inauguration on TV.
The inauguration took about an hour.
The principal gave a speech at the inauguration.
On the day of the inauguration, I received a bouquet.

explain: '취임식'은 새 대통령, 사장, 교장 같은 사람이 일을 시작하는 날 하는 행사예요. 일을 끝내고 떠날 때 하는 행사는 '퇴임식'이에요. 학교에서는 '입학식'과 '졸업식'이 짝이 되는 것처럼 '취임식'과 '퇴임식'도 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The presidential inauguration was shown on television.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 대표적인 취임식으로 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The best-known kind of inauguration, often heard in the news.

phrases.en: Many people attended the inauguration ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 가서 함께한다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual verb pairing for attending the event.

phrases.en: The staff are preparing for the inauguration ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 열기 전에 준비할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting ready for the event beforehand.

explain_en: 취임식 is the ceremony held when a new president, CEO, or principal starts their job. The ceremony for leaving a post is 퇴임식. Just as 입학식 and 졸업식 are a pair at school, 취임식 and 퇴임식 are a pair.

examples.en: I watched the Olympic closing ceremony on TV.
At the closing ceremony, the athletes greeted the audience.
There will be fireworks after the closing ceremony.
Singers performed at the film festival's closing ceremony.
The staff are busy preparing for the closing ceremony.
I waited until late to see the closing ceremony.

explain: 올림픽, 영화제, 체육대회처럼 큰 행사가 끝날 때 하는 공식 행사예요. 반대말은 '개회식'이고, 행사 전체가 아니라 끝날 때의 의식을 가리킬 때 써요.

phrases.en: The film festival closing ceremony is held at 7 p.m.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 끝나는 때를 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to announce when an event wraps up.

phrases.en: The mayor attended the closing ceremony and gave a speech.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 행사에 가는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for going to an official event.

phrases.en: A famous singer performed at the closing ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝날 때 하는 축하 공연을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the celebratory show at the end.

explain_en: Ceremony that closes an event, opposite of the opening. It is the official event held at the end of big events like the Olympics, film festivals and sports days. The opposite is '개회식' (opening ceremony), and it refers to the ceremony at the end rather than the whole event.

examples.en: There is a parking lot at the back of the building.
Please sign the back of the card.
The phone's rear camera is better.
The date was written on the back of the photo.
The rear of the car got scratched a bit.
The front and back designs are very different.

explain: 사물의 뒤쪽 면을 말하는 약간 딱딱한 말이에요. 반대말은 '전면'이고, 일상에서는 '뒷면', '뒤쪽'이라고 더 많이 해요. 설명서, 카드, 건물, 카메라처럼 안내문에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: This phone has a good rear camera.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계의 뒤쪽에 있는 카메라를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the camera on the back of a device.

phrases.en: Please use the rear parking lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 뒤쪽 주차장을 안내문에서 이렇게 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: Signs use this to name the parking lot behind a building.

phrases.en: Please write your name on the back of the card.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후면'과 뜻이 같지만 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '후면' but more common in daily speech.

explain_en: Rear face of a structure or machine — formal, technical register. A slightly formal word for the back side of an object. The opposite is '전면' (front), and in daily speech '뒷면' or '뒤쪽' are more common. You see 후면 in manuals, cards, buildings, and camera descriptions.

gh: flip side of a flat object; plain

p.n: 뒷면 is plainer and sounds like the flip side of a thing.

t90.ax: Please sign the back of the card.

en: a large wad of cash; a bundle of money

examples.en: A huge sum of money left the bank all at once.
He carried a wad of cash around in his bag.
A big chunk of money came in as a year-end bonus.
Large sums of money are flowing into the real estate market.

examples.ko: 갑자기 뭉칫돈이 생기면 어디에 쓸 거예요?
examples.en: If you suddenly got a big pile of money, what would you spend it on?

examples.ko: 계좌에 뭉칫돈이 들어온 이유를 설명해야 했어요.
examples.en: I had to explain why a large sum came into my account.

explain: 한꺼번에 큰돈이 오가거나 한 덩어리로 있는 돈을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '뭉칫돈이 몰리다', '뭉칫돈이 빠져나가다'처럼 자주 나와요. '목돈'과 비슷하지만 뭉칫돈은 한꺼번에 움직이는 큰돈이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: A huge amount of money poured into the new apartments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰돈이 한곳으로 모이는 장면에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when large sums gather in one place.

phrases.en: He withdrew a large sum from the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한꺼번에 많은 돈을 찾을 때 쓰는 뉴스식 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for taking out a lot of cash at once.

phrases.en: I heard a large sum of money changed hands between the two companies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰돈의 거래가 있었다는 말로, 의심스러운 분위기로도 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says big money was exchanged, sometimes with a suspicious tone.

explain_en: It refers to a large sum of money moving all at once or sitting as one lump. In the news it often appears as '뭉칫돈이 몰리다' or '뭉칫돈이 빠져나가다'. It is similar to '목돈', but '뭉칫돈' has a stronger feel of big money moving in one go.

t90.ax: He carried a wad of cash around in his bag.

examples.en: Sales in the fourth quarter rose sharply this year.

examples.ko: 회사는 사분기에 한 해 실적을 정리해요.
examples.en: The company wraps up the year's results in the fourth quarter.
As the fourth quarter began, the winter sale started.

examples.ko: 삼 분기보다 사분기 판매량이 더 많았어요.
examples.en: Sales were higher in the fourth quarter than in the third.
We have to reach the target by the end of the quarter.

examples.ko: 지난 사분기에는 환율 때문에 이익이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Last quarter, profits fell because of the exchange rate.

explain: 글에서는 보통 '4분기'라고 숫자로 쓰고, 읽을 때는 '사 분기'라고 해요. '1분기', '2분기'처럼 순서를 매겨 말하고 주로 회사 실적이나 경제 뉴스에서 나와요.

phrases.en: In the fourth quarter, sales go up because of many year-end events.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글에서는 숫자로 쓰는 것이 일반적이고, 읽을 때는 '사 분기'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usually written with a number, and read aloud as '사 분기'.

phrases.example: 이번 분기 실적이 좋아서 보너스를 받았어요.
phrases.en: This quarter's results were good, so I got a bonus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서 없이 한 분기를 가리킬 때 쓰며, 회사 성과를 말할 때 '실적'과 함께 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a quarter without specifying its number, and often appears with '실적' when talking about company performance.

phrases.en: The company writes a report every quarter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해를 네 번으로 나눈 기간마다 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means doing something in each of the year's four periods.

explain_en: In writing it is usually '4분기' with a number, and it is read as '사 분기'. It is used in sequence like '1분기' and '2분기', mainly in company results and economic news.

examples.en: I complete all my homework.
I finished filling out the application.
When the installation completes, the app opens.
They will finish the construction by today.
A text arrives after you complete the payment.
We finished all preparations and set off.

explain: '끝내다'보다 딱딱하고, 정해진 일이 끝났을 때 써요. 앱 화면에 '완료'라고 뜨는 것도 같은 말이에요. 말할 때는 '다 했어요', '마쳤어요'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Please let me know when you finish the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작업', '등록', '설치'처럼 절차가 있는 일과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits tasks with steps, like work, registration, or installation.

phrases.example: 이 일을 완료하는 데 사흘 걸려요.
phrases.en: It takes three days to complete this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 얼마나 필요한지 말할 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pattern for saying how long something takes.

phrases.en: Please complete the registration by this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 공지에서 정중하게 시킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite instruction often seen in notices.

explain_en: Active; you finish a task, form, or homework (숙제를 완료하다) It is stiffer than '끝내다' and is used when a set task is done. The word '완료' shown on app screens is the same word. In speech, '다 했어요' or '마쳤어요' is more common.

gh: finish a program, without earning a degree

p.n: 완성하다 needs something made into a whole, so it is odd for a task.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝난 기념으로 혼자 자축 파티를 했어요.
examples.en: To mark the end of my exam, I had a little celebration by myself.
I bought a cake to celebrate my own promotion.
Let's have a small celebration among ourselves.

examples.ko: 오늘은 자축의 의미로 좋아하는 음식을 먹어요.
examples.en: Today I'll eat my favorite food to treat myself.

examples.ko: 첫 월급을 받고 자축하며 가족에게 선물을 했어요.
examples.en: After my first paycheck, I celebrated by giving my family gifts.
Something worth celebrating came up, so I called my friends.

explain: '축하'는 보통 남에게 해 주는 것이고, 자축은 나 자신이나 우리끼리 기뻐하는 것에 써요. 보통 '자축하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일상에서는 '셀프 축하'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: We quietly celebrated finishing the project.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자축'을 동사로 쓸 때 가장 많이 쓰는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb form of 자축.

phrases.example: 우리는 합격을 기뻐하며 자축의 건배를 했어요.
phrases.en: We made a toast to ourselves, happy about passing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 위해 기쁨을 나누며 잔을 부딪칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when raising a glass to celebrate one's own success.

phrases.example: 오늘은 월급날이라 셀프 축하로 맛있는 걸 먹었어요.
phrases.en: Today was payday, so I treated myself to something tasty as a self-celebration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '자축'을 가볍게 바꿔 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday way to say 자축.

explain_en: '축하' is usually directed at someone else, while 자축 is celebrating yourself or your own group. It is usually used as the verb '자축하다', and in casual talk people also say '셀프 축하'.

examples.ko: 전전 학기에는 수업을 하나도 듣지 못했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't take a single class the semester before last.

examples.ko: 전전 팀장님은 지금 다른 회사에 계세요.
examples.en: The team leader before the last one is now at a different company.

examples.ko: 전전 회사에서 만난 동료와 지금도 연락해요.
examples.en: I still keep in touch with a coworker from the company before my last one.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 전전 주인이 운영할 때가 더 인기 있었어요.
examples.en: That shop was more popular when the owner before the last one ran it.
That's something we already talked about at the meeting before last.

examples.ko: 저는 전전 직장에서 처음 디자인 일을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I first learned design work at the job before my last one.

explain: '바로 전의 그 전'이라는 순서를 나타내는 관형사라서 뒤에 명사가 와요. '전전날', '전전달'처럼 한 단어로 굳은 말도 있어요. 말할 때는 '지지난주', '지지난달'처럼 '지지난'을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I met a friend for the first time in a while the week before last.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전전주' 대신 일상에서 훨씬 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used far more than 전전주 in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 전전날에 비가 와서 길이 아직 젖어 있어요.
phrases.en: It rained the day before yesterday, so the road is still wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전전'이 붙어 한 단어로 굳은 말이에요. 어제의 전날을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed word built with 전전, meaning the day before yesterday.

phrases.example: 전전달에 이사를 해서 아직 짐이 많아요.
phrases.en: I moved two months ago, so I still have a lot of boxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난달의 전 달을 가리키는 말이고, 말할 때는 '지지난달'도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the month before last month. In speech, 지지난달 is also common.

explain_en: It is a determiner showing the one before the previous one, so a noun follows it. There are also fixed words such as '전전날' and '전전달'. In speech, '지지난' as in '지지난주' and '지지난달' is used more.

en: to be aggregated; to be collected

examples.en: Many opinions are brought together into one.
The survey content was summed up in the report.
It is easy to understand when you look at the combined results.
When all materials are collected, they will be put together.
Each class's scores are being totaled.
The opinions were put together, and the presentation started.

explain: 여러 가지가 모여 하나로 정리될 때 써요. 단순히 숫자를 더하는 '합하다'보다 내용을 정리해서 묶는 느낌이에요. 보고서와 발표, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The survey results are put together in one table.
phrases.nuance_ko: '종합되다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이라 말할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more spoken way to say 종합되다.

phrases.example: 모든 내용이 한 장에 종합되어 있어요.
phrases.en: All the contents are compiled on one page.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 정리가 끝난 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being compiled.

phrases.en: The data hasn't been compiled yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정리가 아직 안 끝났을 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form used when the compiling is not finished.

explain_en: Used when many things come together into one organized whole. Unlike simple adding, it suggests sorting content and bundling it. It is common in reports, presentations and the news.

en: to be progressed; to be advanced; to make progress

examples.en: The negotiations are moving forward little by little.
I am worried because things are not moving ahead quickly.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 진전되면 무역도 늘 거예요.
examples.en: If relations between the two countries advance, trade will grow too.
I will announce the results after the investigation has progressed.

examples.ko: 수사가 진전되어서 범인이 곧 잡힐 것 같아요.
examples.en: The investigation has advanced, so the culprit will probably be caught soon.
Every time the discussion progressed, the mood got better.

explain: 협상, 수사, 관계처럼 일이 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 일이 주어예요. 사람이 나아질 때는 '발전하다', '나아지다'가 자연스러워요. '진전이 있다', '진전이 없다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: There has been a little progress in the research.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '진전'으로 일이 나아졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 진전 to say that things have moved forward.

phrases.en: Even with meetings, there is no progress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 앞으로 나아가지 않을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when things are not moving forward.

phrases.en: Relations between the two countries advanced quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빠르게'를 붙이면 일이 빨리 나아간다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 빠르게 makes clear that things are advancing quickly.

explain_en: A matter or relationship moves ahead; slightly formal. It is used when a matter such as negotiations, an investigation, or a relationship moves forward, so the subject is the matter itself. When a person improves, '발전하다' or '나아지다' sounds more natural. People also often say '진전이 있다' or '진전이 없다' (there is or is no progress).

t90.ax: The negotiations are moving forward little by little.
